$comment: Machine-readable version of v5/DECORATION_VS_STRUCTURE.md three-question test.

three_question_test.question: What job does this element do?
valid_answers_examples: marks the boundary between the editorial section and the reference index
separates the primary CTA from the secondary
contains the media so the caption reads as belonging to the image
signals the state change from draft to published
invalid_answers_examples: matches the rest of the page
gives the page a technical feel

three_question_test.question: What breaks if it is removed?
three_question_test.structural_if: understanding, hierarchy, or comprehension is lost
three_question_test.decorative_if: only finish or polish is lost - nothing communicative changes

three_question_test.question: Is a stronger structural device already doing the same job?
three_question_test.if_yes: remove the element - it is redundant

structural_elements: deliberate surface changes that communicate mode change
state indicators that show something IS something
commonly_decorative_elements: dividers, hairlines, hr - decorative by default
corner brackets, register marks, viewfinder marks
background grid overlays without work to do
metadata pills that do not filter or link
radial gradient auras without light/focus semantics
glass panels without a scene behind them
fake terminals, fake dashboards, fake code windows

steps: list every decorative element on the page
note which deletions caused a real loss
for real losses, decide whether a stronger structural device should carry that job instead

final_test: mark every visible element S (structural) or D (decorative). Ratio strongly toward S with small number of well-placed D items is healthy. Ratio toward D or heavy D noise between S elements means decoration is doing too much of the work.
